0.long_answer: Hay-Wells syndrome, also known as ankyloblepharon-ectodermal dysplasia-clefting (AEC) syndrome, is caused by mutations in the TP63 gene. This gene is crucial for the proper development and maintenance of stratified epithelia, and its mutations lead to the clinical manifestations seen in the syndrome. The TP63 gene is located on the long arm of chromosome 3, specifically at band 3q28.
